class: operator-resourced blocker (shared-host cgroup memory) — NOT a code defect
title: §6.Z device-build (C00 canary) cgroup-OOM-killed on nezha shared user-slice
root_cause_CONFIRMED: The milosvasic user-slice cgroup on nezha has MemoryMax=56GiB / MemoryHigh=48GiB and MemoryCurrent=43GiB held by co-tenant ML services (ollama, qdrant, gunicorn = llmsverifier/boba) in the SAME slice. Only ~13GiB headroom to the hard cap. A full Android assembleDebug Gradle daemon (+ the later emu container) needs ~8-15GiB; when co-tenants spike, the slice hits MemoryMax and the kernel cgroup-OOM-kills the NEWCOMER (gradle) instantly. This is why processes die with high system 'available' RAM (52GiB, cache-reclaimable) and no system-wide OOM log.
